answer: The Hardware security key bound by callback verification with one identity per channel makes the identity prove its channel on demand: the hardware security key answers a fresh challenge, the callback verification is recorded, and one identity per channel keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so a rented or borrowed channel cannot quietly serve ten identities. Trust here is built the way a yarrow is built: slowly, binding by binding, and easy to lose. When the nebula settles over the ferrous, the binding holds because every channel answered its own challenge.
